assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only medalist:inori-yuitsuka@manga#provisional-character-monograph (the canonical provisional character monograph, version 1.2, INDEPENDENT_SOURCE_FIDELITY_REVIEWED) and medalist:inori-yuitsuka@manga#coach-and-pupil-relationship-study (the canonical coach-and-pupil relationship study, version 1.1, with its 2026-10-14 original-language addendum) at basis_commit, both read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the Japanese manga V01-V15 (Scores 1-61) to the warm-up before the Junior Grand Prix Final free skate, combined freeze MD-FR-FB02, with Official Fanbooks 01 and 02 as creator-layer supplements kept separate and used for no grade. The frozen readings, the seven ledgers, the readiness rows, the speech and interlocutor audit, the source-fidelity audit and the Tsukasa Akeuraji monograph are not curated evidence on this subject, and nothing is borrowed from them. The syntheses' confidence labels and the project's 'no model' readiness record are inputs, not conclusions. The animated adaptation, English editions, parody chapters and anything after Score 61 are excluded, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: From V01 (age eleven, hidden self-teaching, MD-EV-V01-0004) through the V15 warm-up before the Junior Grand Prix Final free skate (December of her first middle-school year, age thirteen, MD-EV-V15-0052). V03 is split at the shin injury and the train-home acceptance (MD-EV-V03-0032, MD-EV-V03-0040) and the deadline set in anger (MD-EV-V03-0055); V04 at the farewell to the cold feeling (MD-EV-V04-0038); V09 at the unilateral layout change (MD-EV-V09-0030) and the division by audience after the result (MD-EV-V09-0040, -0043, -0048); V13 at the short-program failure (MD-EV-V13-0004-0008), the truancy and platform (MD-EV-V13-0034, -0040) and the bench (MD-EV-V13-0044-0046); and V15 at the press statement (MD-EV-V15-0016), the evening with her mother (MD-EV-V15-0046), the stairwell (MD-EV-V15-0048-0051) and the warm-up. The eight months between V09 and V10 and the year inside V03 are largely unshown. No default state is set; one must be selected, and no state after the warm-up is established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph gives a specialist account of Inori (Inori Yuitsuka): her place on the ice held as a permission that results must justify (conditional tenure, MD-CL-0001@15), with competence, agency and candour growing on that unchanged premise; two modes, attentive and compelled, of which the first governs execution and recovery and the second has decided one competition choice (MD-EV-V09-0030; MD-CL-0015@8, @14); a habit of reading adults' faces first and assigning the cause to herself (MD-CL-0028@5, HIGH for the mechanism); concealment for another's sake, specifically of whatever would show Tsukasa (Tsukasa Akeuraji), her coach, what she thinks she costs him (relationship study, concealment table); and provoked commitments aloud before people above her. It predicts some of her mistakes: training through pain (MD-EV-V03-0032), the unilateral triple Axel, the V13 truancy (MD-EV-V13-0034). B would overclaim: both syntheses decline an operational model; at the boundary the monograph says the evidence cannot choose whether the December vow, the creed or the new stairwell test governs (MD-RD-0072), cannot say whether the chosen role is agency or the old compulsion in a composed voice (MD-CL-0015@14), and leaves the wish to carry and the wish to vanish undistinguished among three compatible readings (MD-OQ-V15-03). Being unable to tell which competing motive decides is insufficiency, not productive uncertainty. The compelled mode's decisive role rests on one competition instance, and whether the premise is a standing self-understanding or a mood of evaluative occasions is MODERATE. D would understate an independently source-reviewed account with explicit claims, counterevidence and discriminating tests that supports narrow extrapolation.

The monograph orders Inori (Inori Yuitsuka)'s development by phase from V01 (age eleven, hidden self-teaching, MD-EV-V01-0004) to the V15 warm-up (age thirteen), with event keys, a competition record and the claims ledger's version history, and says what changed and what did not: the deficit named and bidden farewell (MD-EV-V02-0030; MD-EV-V04-0038), the measure moving to Hikaru (Hikaru Kamisaki) (V05-V06), both modes in one skate and the belief disclosed (V07-V09), the self-reliance rule and the claim on risk (V10-V12), the V13 collapse, truancy and bench, the V14 film read as her own story, and the three V15 statements. The relationship study adds the directional knowledge history across the same phases. It records its own withdrawn V13 reading and the evidence that withdrew it (MD-RV-0259, MD-RV-0261). C would understate a located, causally ordered developmental record with explicit corrections. A is rejected: the eight months between V09 and V10 and the year inside V03 are largely unshown, the Bangkok free skate and the Event 7 win are reported only, and the state after the stairwell is not established.

The evidence records located written-Japanese findings for Inori (Inori Yuitsuka), not sound: 私 or わたし and 司先生 with polite requests to Tsukasa (Tsukasa Akeuraji), with plain exceptions such as 先生も信じてる？ (MD-EV-V06-0003); plain よ and さ to her mother, Nozomi (Nozomi Yuitsuka), switching to 大丈夫です when Tsukasa arrives (MD-EV-V15-0046); formal grammar carrying an uncompromising refusal; and a located key vocabulary by volume (選べる, 証明, 期待される, 本気, ずるい, 恥ずかしい, 負担, 報いる, 許してもらえた, 役目, 冷たい気持ち). The relationship study's addendum adds that respectful address coexists with plain grammar and direct disagreement. B would overclaim: the monograph states these are not a frequency census or response rule, the speech and interlocutor audit that owns the diagnostic examples is outside the set, dialogue elsewhere is paraphrased, and no morphology system or state deltas are given. D would understate a located interlocutor contrast and lexicon.

The monograph says the corpus is thin on Inori (Inori Yuitsuka)'s life away from evaluation and makes no claim about her temperament outside the settings shown. What it locates is consistent: losing and forgetting things with self-reproach, sometimes comic (MD-EV-V03-0006, MD-EV-V11-0051, MD-EV-V14-0002, MD-EV-V14-0004); worms as a private resource since age seven (MD-EV-V02-0036, MD-EV-V04-0037); giving away her own sweets (MD-EV-V11-0013); eating with her team and asking for a treat while performing cheer (MD-EV-V13-0002, MD-EV-V13-0007); and making friends across rivalry (MD-EV-V11-0039). C would overclaim: school appears mainly as a difficulty or a rule she breaks, and no ordinary-life driver is stated beyond self-reproach. E would understate located instances that recur across volumes.

The evidence conditions Inori (Inori Yuitsuka)'s conduct by partner. Toward Tsukasa (Tsukasa Akeuraji): managed disclosure that withholds only what would show him what she costs him, while disclosing much else (relationship study, MD-RL-0048, MD-RL-0068, MD-RL-0113, MD-RL-0152); speech she can hear as a verdict not arriving while she conceals, indirect forms arriving (a conditional rule, not a trait); reading his face first; and his standing as her stake from V08. Toward her mother, Nozomi (Nozomi Yuitsuka): performed contentment after a loss, and the only person told the wish to vanish (MD-RL-0358). Toward Mika (Mika Yuitsuka), her sister: protective and the keeper of her grief. Toward Hikaru (Hikaru Kamisaki): friend, then the measure she cannot face after failing. Toward Okazaki Iruka, Karasuba Daria and Ryoka Miketa: open, quick to repair and unresentful. The monograph names the contrast, open with peers and bright but guarded with caring adults, as one of the corpus's firmer findings. C would understate partner-specific discrimination with a dedicated directional study. A is rejected: what the stairwell changed is open in effect, the Tsukasa rule about indirect instruction is untested once nothing is concealed, and relations other than Tsukasa rest on the monograph's shorter sections.

Interior states of Inori (Inori Yuitsuka) are located through her captions and self-accounts and kept apart from adults' inferences: the V09 free-skate captions giving her belief that becoming Tsukasa's pupil ended his dream (MD-EV-V09-0031; MD-KN-0083); her V11 night account to Okazaki Iruka (MD-EV-V11-0034-0036); the V13 fear of being thought not in earnest (MD-EV-V13-0008) and the disclosed inward disparagement (MD-EV-V13-0045); the V14 captions; and the three V15 statements, set against the account of Kanayumi Miho, the trainer, whose phrase about the sacrifice of Tsukasa (Tsukasa Akeuraji)'s life the evidence marks as Kanayumi's inference (MD-KN-0145-0147). C would understate located interior states with explicit attribution of whose account each is. A is rejected: whether she still holds the older belief that she ended Tsukasa's skating is not shown, the inward disparagement is disclosed but not explained, and the two V15 wishes are left unrelated.

Conflict conduct of Inori (Inori Yuitsuka) is located: disagreement with Tsukasa (Tsukasa Akeuraji) on reasons, held and prevailing (MD-EV-V08-0027); overriding him inside a program (MD-EV-V09-0030); deception by degrees (MD-EV-V13-0034); rage and the refused train on the platform (MD-EV-V13-0040); a refusal to Okazaki Iruka in formal grammar; the stairwell claim that she will not be treated as weak (MD-EV-V15-0048); and, at her first competition, telling her mother she wants to win and lose as an athlete after overhearing a request that her jumps be made easy (MD-EV-V02-0005-0006). B would overclaim: no general conflict pattern is stated, the conduct is mostly toward Tsukasa, and how she meets conflict after the stairwell is untested. D would understate located instances across volumes with their triggers.

The evidence offers local ethically relevant choices by Inori (Inori Yuitsuka) rather than an account of her moral reasoning: refusing a caught wish that others would fail (MD-EV-V11-0025), a stated principle against hurting people without knowing it (MD-EV-V15-0013) beside a year of keeping Tsukasa (Tsukasa Akeuraji) ignorant, which the page does not connect, and the claim to bear a cost whoever suffers (MD-EV-V15-0048). The discovery row claims no ethics dimension, and the monograph analyzes none. D would overclaim a distributed account the set does not give. This grade bounds use; it is not a finding about the character.

The monograph notes comic self-reproach, a comic misreading of Tsukasa (Tsukasa Akeuraji)'s face (MD-EV-V14-0004) and that Inori (Inori Yuitsuka) is glad and playful throughout, and treats her delight in learning as counterevidence to the thesis (MD-EV-V04-0038, MD-EV-V09-0028, MD-EV-V10-0030). It gives no account of her humor or play. D would overclaim analysis the set does not contain.

The two syntheses cover Inori (Inori Yuitsuka) across every volume to Score 61, citing event, knowledge, relationship and claim keys from the frozen readings and seven ledgers, with fanbook material confined to labeled creator-layer sections. The monograph is independently source-fidelity reviewed. B would overclaim: the keys resolve to ledgers and readings outside the set, the relationship study states it rests on the readings' and ledgers' paraphrases and did not inspect pages, the speech and interlocutor audit is outside the set, and the series is ongoing with a boundary inside a competition. D would understate complete phase-by-phase coverage routed to stable keys.

The evidence affirmatively bounds Inori (Inori Yuitsuka): it states what it does not claim (a cause for the November collapse, any diagnosis, formation by deprivation, that the film's ending describes her and Tsukasa (Tsukasa Akeuraji), that the stairwell lifted or failed to lift her burden, whether she still holds the older belief, anything about her temperament outside sport); records that recovery inside a program after a real error is unshown since the aim was set (MD-CL-0019@12); withdraws its own V13 reading on V15 evidence (MD-RV-0259, MD-RV-0261); bounds the indirect-instruction rule as conditional; and keeps creator-layer material out of every trait. C would understate explicit, located affirmative limits and corrections. A is rejected: several bounds are absences of evidence rather than located contradictions.

States of Inori (Inori Yuitsuka) are located by volume, event key and age, with the competition record dated by event, the V15 evening split into the press statement, the evening with her mother, the stairwell and the warm-up, and the boundary fixed in the six-minute warm-up before the Junior Grand Prix Final free skate. C would understate this located sequence. A is rejected: two long intervals are largely unshown and two results are reported rather than depicted.

conditions: Illustrative textual Japanese only, never quotation, and only toward Tsukasa (Tsukasa Akeuraji) or her mother, Nozomi (Nozomi Yuitsuka): 私 or わたし and 司先生 with polite requests to Tsukasa and only occasional plain contracted questions of the attested kind (MD-EV-V06-0003); plain よ and さ to her mother.
Key words are used only in the state where the evidence places them (for example 証明 in the V10 creed, 本気 in V13, 負担 and 報いる in V15); no catchphrase or verbal tic is invented.
Politeness does not imply agreement: formal grammar can carry a refusal.
No dialogue toward other interlocutors, no acoustic or anime performance, and no line set after the V15 warm-up.
scenario_readiness.note: Located address, first-person forms and an interlocutor contrast constrain short illustrative lines for Inori (Inori Yuitsuka) toward Tsukasa (Tsukasa Akeuraji) and her mother only. The missing morphology and the uncurated speech audit keep the use narrow.

conditions: Predictions are limited to the mechanisms the evidence establishes: attentive-mode execution with sensation inventory and single instructions; concealment of what would show Tsukasa her cost; provoked commitments aloud before people above her; good deliberation when given branches; reading an adult's face and taking its cause on herself.
Whether a decision under pressure goes to the attentive or the compelled mode is presented as uncertain; one competition instance does not make the compelled override a rule.
At the V15 boundary, competing readings (the December vow, the creed, the stairwell test; the wish to carry and the wish to vanish) are presented, not resolved.
No outcome of the free skate or anything after Score 61 is generated.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One explicitly selected state from V01 through the V15 evening before the stairwell: V01; V02-V04 (V03 before or after the shin injury and train-home acceptance, MD-EV-V03-0032/0040); V05-V06; V07-V09 (V09 before or after the layout change, MD-EV-V09-0030); V10-V12; V13 before or after the bench (MD-EV-V13-0044-0046); V14 short program; or V15 before the stairwell. The post-stairwell state is excluded.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Tsukasa (Tsukasa Akeuraji) in the coach-pupil relation the study samples; her mother, Nozomi (Nozomi Yuitsuka), or sister, Mika (Mika Yuitsuka); peers Okazaki Iruka, Hikaru (Hikaru Kamisaki), Karasuba Daria or Ryoka Miketa in their sampled registers. Transfer to an unfamiliar adult whose face she cannot read is untested and excluded.
setting_constraints: Figure-skating training, competition, travel and family settings of the kinds shown.
No school life, ordinary leisure or social setting outside skating beyond the sampled items.
No recovery after a real error inside a program is modeled as known.

scenario_readiness.note: The established mechanisms support narrow extrapolation for Inori (Inori Yuitsuka) in sampled skating and coaching situations at a selected state before the stairwell. The evidence's own refusal to choose a governing state after the stairwell excludes that state.

The monograph says the corpus is thin on Inori (Inori Yuitsuka)'s life away from evaluation and makes no claim about her temperament outside the settings shown. The located items do not support extrapolation to ordinary social scenes.

The evidence gives local ethically relevant choices by Inori (Inori Yuitsuka) but no account of her moral reasoning, and the discovery row claims no ethics dimension. Ethical deliberation in a new situation would be invention.
Inori (Inori Yuitsuka) is eleven to thirteen within the boundary, and the evidence analyzes no romance. Nothing is established, so no readiness is claimed.

conditions: Sampled classes only: training sessions, quotas and drills; competition warm-ups and segments; choosing layouts with branches set out; responses to scores and placements; travel to competitions; requests and disagreements with Tsukasa about plans.

She trains through pain and must be rationed; she can separate a defeat with visible causes from a defeat at full strength, which she cannot bear (MD-EV-V11-0040); her competence is scored and not a guarantee (MD-PERF-0107).
No free-skate result, post-Score-61 career, federation politics or recovery inside a program after an error is generated.
scenario_readiness.note: Competitive skating is Inori (Inori Yuitsuka)'s working context, and the evidence samples training, competition and the coaching relation densely enough for bounded extrapolation at a selected state before the stairwell.

known_limits.statement: The boundary for Inori (Inori Yuitsuka) falls in the six-minute warm-up before the Junior Grand Prix Final free skate (MD-FR-FB02, Score 61). The series is ongoing, the result is not known, and anything after Score 61 is outside the evidence.

After the V15 stairwell the evidence cannot choose whether the December vow, the creed or the new test of bearing only what she can call her own life governs Inori (Inori Yuitsuka)'s conduct, and records whether the chosen role is agency or the old compulsion as open (MD-RD-0072; MD-CL-0015@14). It also leaves the older belief that she ended Tsukasa (Tsukasa Akeuraji)'s skating neither voiced nor withdrawn (MD-KN-0147).

Inori (Inori Yuitsuka)'s wish to carry everything (to Tsukasa (Tsukasa Akeuraji)) and her wish to vanish into the gifted double (to her mother, Nozomi (Nozomi Yuitsuka)) are said the same evening and left unrelated; three readings remain compatible with the page (MD-OQ-V15-03), and Tsukasa has not been told of the second (MD-KN-0148).

Both curated syntheses explicitly offer no operational model of Inori (Inori Yuitsuka); the project's readiness rows record a bounded provisional monograph and no model. Any conditional rule used under this record is a bounded extrapolation from established mechanisms, not a rule the evidence proposes.

Statements about Inori (Inori Yuitsuka) by adults, notably the trainer Kanayumi Miho's account that she skates at the sacrifice of Tsukasa (Tsukasa Akeuraji)'s life and as punishment, and the unadopted hypothesis that her capacities were formed under deprivation (MD-CL-0028@5), are not her account and are not used as her interior.
How Inori (Inori Yuitsuka) meets a real error inside a program since the V13 aim of getting up was set is unshown (MD-CL-0019@12); V14 shows a recovered jump under reproduced conditions only.
The evidence is thin on Inori (Inori Yuitsuka)'s life away from evaluation and makes no claim about her temperament outside the settings shown (MD-CL-0015@1).
Official Fanbook 01 and 02 material, including the conceptions of Mika's and Nozomi's histories and working drafts, is creator-layer context; no trait or grade in this record rests on it.

The relationship study rests on the readings' and ledgers' paraphrases and did not inspect pages; both syntheses route to ledger keys whose bodies, together with the speech and interlocutor audit and the source-fidelity audit, are outside the curated set.
No held-out validation, probe set or speech census is part of the curated evidence; generated dialogue is illustrative and its accuracy is untested.
